scenes.say: Paula and Sam both earn 64,064 dollars, but only one gets the bigger house.
A common guideline caps all debt at 36 percent of gross pay, or 1,922 dollars here.

visual.label: 36% of the median monthly salary, for all debt

scenes.say: Paula's new car costs 787 dollars a month, and Sam's used car costs 582.
Subtract the car, and Paula keeps 1,135 dollars for housing while Sam keeps 1,340.
At 7.21 percent, their ceilings land near 125,500 and 153,300 dollars.
So a 205 dollar car gap moved the house by 27,748 dollars on the same salary.
The other four salary levels, from 32,968 to 151,788, are in the full video on the channel.
